title: Ellice Islands Vote to Separate from Gilbert Islands
description: Polynesian Ellice Islanders voted overwhelmingly in a 1974 referendum to separate from the Micronesian Gilbert Islands, with formal separation taking effect on 1 October 1975. The split reflected ethnic and political differences and set the stage for independence as Tuvalu and Kiribati respectively.

title: Tuvalu Achieves Independence from United Kingdom
description: Tuvalu gained independence from Britain on 1 October 1978, becoming a Commonwealth realm with Queen Elizabeth II as head of state and Toaripi Lauti as the first Prime Minister. The new nation entered the international system as one of the smallest sovereign states by population in the world.

title: Treaty of Friendship Resolves US Atoll Claims
description: Tuvalu and the United States signed a Treaty of Friendship in February 1979 under which Washington renounced its claims to four atolls (Funafuti, Nukufetau, Nukulaelae, and Niutao) inherited from the 1856 Guano Act. The treaty entered into force in 1983 and removed the last territorial overhang of the 19th century US claims.

title: Tuvalu Establishes Diplomatic Relations with Taiwan
description: Tuvalu recognised the Republic of China (Taiwan) in 1979, with full embassies opening in the early 1980s, joining a small group of Pacific states maintaining ties with Taipei. The relationship has underpinned major Taiwanese aid and technical cooperation programmes for over four decades.

title: Tuvaluans Vote to Retain the Monarchy
description: A 1986 referendum saw Tuvaluans vote to retain the British monarchy as head of state rather than become a republic. The result confirmed continuing constitutional ties with the Crown, in contrast to the path taken by some other Commonwealth Pacific states.

title: Tuvalu Adopts New National Flag Without Union Jack
description: Tuvalu briefly removed the Union Jack from its flag in 1995 under Prime Minister Kamuta Latasi as a symbol of independent identity, before reinstating it in 1997 after a change of government. The episode highlighted continuing debate over post-colonial symbolism.

title: Tuvalu Signs Landmark .tv Domain Deal Worth USD 50 Million
description: In 2000 Tuvalu signed a 12-year deal with the Idealab subsidiary later acquired by VeriSign, leasing rights to its .tv internet domain for around USD 50 million in guaranteed payments. The windfall, equivalent to several years of GDP, funded paved roads, the UN admission, schools, and the country's first national stock exchange contribution.

title: Tuvalu Admitted to the United Nations
description: Tuvalu was admitted to the United Nations on 5 September 2000 as the 189th member state, with funds from the .tv domain deal helping cover the costs of UN dues and a permanent mission. UN membership amplified Tuvalu's international voice on climate change.

title: Tuvalu Calls for Climate Refugee Resettlement
description: Prime Minister Koloa Talake formally raised the prospect of large-scale resettlement of Tuvaluans in Australia and New Zealand due to climate change at the UN General Assembly. The intervention helped place small island climate vulnerability on the global diplomatic agenda.

title: Tuvalu Threatens to Sue United States and Australia Over Climate Change
description: The government in 2002 publicly considered legal action in the International Court of Justice against the United States and Australia for failing to ratify the Kyoto Protocol. The threat helped frame Tuvalu's identity as an early international climate plaintiff.

title: Maatia Toafa Government Falls After No-Confidence Vote
description: Prime Minister Maatia Toafa lost a no-confidence vote in December 2010 after just months in office, replaced by Willy Telavi. The episode illustrated the inherent fragility of governments in a parliament of 15 members.

title: Tuvaluan Constitutional Crisis Over Governor-General
description: Prime Minister Willy Telavi refused to convene parliament in mid-2013 amid no-confidence pressure, prompting Governor-General Iakoba Italeli to dismiss him in August 2013. The intervention was a rare colonial-era reserve power use that resolved the crisis and brought Enele Sopoaga to office.

title: First Successful Climate-Change Refugee Case in New Zealand
description: A Tuvaluan family was granted residency in New Zealand in 2014 in a case widely reported as the first time climate change was a contributing factor accepted by an immigration tribunal. While decided primarily on humanitarian grounds, the ruling was a precedent in international migration law.

title: Cyclone Pam Devastates Tuvalu
description: Tropical Cyclone Pam, while passing east of Tuvalu in March 2015, generated severe storm surges that affected nearly half the population and damaged or destroyed homes on Nui, Nukufetau, and other atolls. The disaster forced a rare nationwide state of emergency and international relief response.

title: Tuvalu Hosts Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting
description: Tuvalu prepared to host the Pacific Islands Forum leaders' meeting in 2019, with Prime Minister Enele Sopoaga emphasising climate emergency throughout 2017-2019 preparations. The Forum positioning cemented Tuvalu's role as a leading climate diplomatic voice.

title: Pacific Islands Forum in Funafuti Produces Kainaki II Declaration
description: Pacific leaders meeting in Funafuti in August 2019 adopted the Kainaki II Declaration calling climate change the single greatest threat to Pacific security and demanding deep emissions cuts. The summit highlighted tense exchanges between Pacific leaders and Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison on coal.

title: Kausea Natano Becomes Prime Minister
description: Kausea Natano was elected Prime Minister by parliament in September 2019, narrowly defeating incumbent Enele Sopoaga. The change of leadership produced subtle shifts in foreign policy emphasis, notably on Taiwan ties.

title: Foreign Minister Simon Kofe Delivers Knee-Deep Speech
description: Foreign Minister Simon Kofe addressed the COP26 climate summit in November 2021 standing knee-deep in seawater at a former Tuvaluan beach, delivering a viral speech on rising seas. The image became one of the defining symbols of the climate vulnerability of small island developing states.

title: Tuvalu Announces Plans for Digital Twin Nation
description: At COP27 in November 2022, Tuvalu announced plans to create a digital replica of its territory in the metaverse to preserve culture and statehood as physical land may become uninhabitable. The proposal pushed novel international legal questions about the persistence of statehood after territorial loss.

title: Australia and Tuvalu Sign Falepili Union Treaty
description: Prime Ministers Anthony Albanese and Kausea Natano signed the Falepili Union treaty on 9 November 2023, providing for permanent climate-displacement migration pathways for Tuvaluans to Australia and joint security commitments. The agreement is widely regarded as the world's first bilateral climate-mobility treaty.

title: Constitutional Amendment Affirms Permanence of Tuvaluan Statehood
description: Tuvalu amended its constitution in 2023 to declare that the state and its sovereignty persist regardless of physical changes to its territory due to climate change. The amendment is the first known constitutional provision globally addressing climate-induced loss of land in international law.

title: Tuvalu Holds 2024 General Election
description: Tuvalu held its general election on 26 January 2024, returning a fragmented parliament with no clear majority and leading to defeat for incumbent Prime Minister Kausea Natano. Coalition negotiations produced a new government within weeks.

title: Feleti Teo Elected Prime Minister
description: Former Pacific fisheries leader Feleti Teo was unexpectedly elected Prime Minister by parliament in February 2024, having only just been elected to a parliamentary seat. Teo signalled intent to retain Taiwan ties and review the Falepili Union with Australia.

title: Tuvalu Reviews Falepili Union Provisions
description: The new Teo government reviewed the Australia-Tuvalu Falepili Union, particularly clauses giving Australia a consultative role in third-country security agreements. After consultations, both governments confirmed continuation of the treaty in mid-2024.

title: Tuvalu Reaffirms Diplomatic Recognition of Taiwan
description: Prime Minister Teo publicly reaffirmed Tuvalu's recognition of Taiwan in 2024 amid speculation it might switch to Beijing following the China switches by Solomon Islands, Kiribati, and Nauru. The reaffirmation kept Tuvalu among Taiwan's dwindling group of formal diplomatic partners.

title: First Tuvaluans Apply Under Falepili Union Mobility Pathway
description: The first cohort of Tuvaluans applied for permanent migration to Australia under the Falepili Union climate-mobility ballot in 2025. The applications marked the operational launch of the world's first climate-displacement treaty mechanism.

title: Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project Expands Funafuti Land Reclamation
description: The Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project, financed by the Green Climate Fund, expanded reclaimed land on Funafuti by several hectares to provide elevated areas above projected sea-level rise. The works represent the principal in-country adaptation strategy alongside the Falepili migration pathway.
